relationship.statement: A pendulum's swing period depends on its length and gravity, not on the bob's mass. Larger release angles widen the arc, raise peak speed, and slightly lengthen the period beyond the small-angle estimate.
assumptions: Air resistance and pivot friction are neglected.
The string is massless, taut, and inextensible.
Gravity is held fixed at 9.81 m/s^2; the formula assumes small angles.

quantities.label: String length
quantities.meaning: Distance from the fixed pivot to the center of the pendulum bob.

quantities.label: Release angle
quantities.meaning: Initial angle pulled away from the vertical equilibrium line.

quantities.label: Bob mass
quantities.meaning: Mass of the pendulum bob; alters kinetic energy without changing period.

quantities.label: Gravity
quantities.meaning: Downward gravitational acceleration held constant at Earth's surface.

quantities.label: Period
quantities.meaning: Time required for one complete back-and-forth oscillation.

quantities.label: Frequency
quantities.meaning: Number of complete back-and-forth swings completed each second.

quantities.label: Current angle
quantities.meaning: Instantaneous angular position measured from the vertical downward axis.

quantities.label: Peak speed
quantities.meaning: Maximum tangential speed as the bob crosses the bottom of its arc.

math.code: function compute(inputs, t) { const g = 9.81; const L = inputs.length; const deg0 = inputs.release_angle; const m = inputs.mass; const theta0 = deg0 * Math.PI / 180; const k = Math.sin(theta0 * 0.5); const w0 = Math.sqrt(g / L); const aArr = [1]; const cArr = [k]; let a = 1; let b = Math.sqrt(1 - k * k); const N = 6; for (let i = 0; i < N; i++) { const an = 0.5 * (a + b); const bn = Math.sqrt(a * b); const cn = 0.5 * (a - b); a = an; b = bn; aArr.push(a); cArr.push(cn); } const period = (2 * Math.PI / w0) / a; const frequency = 1 / period; const max_speed = 2 * Math.sqrt(g * L) * k; const u = w0 * t; let phi = (1 << N) * a * u; for (let i = N; i >= 1; i--) { const ratio = (cArr[i] / aArr[i]) * Math.sin(phi); const clamped = ratio > 1 ? 1 : (ratio < -1 ? -1 : ratio); phi = 0.5 * (phi + Math.asin(clamped)); } const sn = Math.sin(phi); const cn = Math.cos(phi); const dn = Math.sqrt(Math.max(1e-12, 1 - k * k * sn * sn)); const cd = cn / dn; const arg = Math.max(-1, Math.min(1, k * cd)); const theta = 2 * Math.asin(arg); const angle = theta * 180 / Math.PI; const refTheta = theta0 * Math.cos(w0 * t); const small_angle_deg = refTheta * 180 / Math.PI; const bob_x = L * Math.sin(theta); const bob_y = -L * Math.cos(theta); const ref_x = L * Math.sin(refTheta); const ref_y = -L * Math.cos(refTheta); const neg_length = -L; const weightLen = 0.55 + 0.08 * m; const weight_tip_y = bob_y - weightLen; const bob_size = 0.25 + 0.7 * ((m - 0.5) / 4.5); return { period: period, frequency: frequency, angle: angle, max_speed: max_speed, small_angle_deg: small_angle_deg, bob_x: bob_x, bob_y: bob_y, ref_x: ref_x, ref_y: ref_y, neg_length: neg_length, weight_tip_y: weight_tip_y, bob_size: bob_size, is_small_angle: deg0 <= 15, is_large_angle: deg0 > 40 }; }

always: Mass alters weight, not the period.

cases.text: Large angle: period lags behind T0.

lesson.title: What changes a pendulum swing?
lesson.description: Adjust string length, release angle, and bob mass to see how each alters the swing. Compare the real pendulum against the small-angle curve over time.
lesson.instructions: Change string length, release angle, and bob mass with the sliders, and scrub time to inspect the arc and period lag.
lesson.goal: Pendulum period depends on string length and slightly on large release angles, never on bob mass, while peak speed grows with both length and angle.
